t: Look up at the long relief along Aldersgate Street. This is The Gold Smelters, also called the Barbican Frieze, or Bryer's Frieze. It was carved by J. Daymond, and the sculptors John Daymond the third and John Dudley Daymond are both credited with making it. The frieze was saved from a building demolished in the 1960s. The Corporation of London re-erected it on this spot in 1975.
